mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo XC40 T4 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A B4204T47 replacement typically costs £1,600-£3,800 supply-only, depending on condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt). Full supply & fit through a specialist adds approximately £600-£1,000 in labour. Used B4204T47: £900-£1,600. Reconditioned B4204T47: £1,600-£2,800. Rebuilt B4204T47: £2,400-£3,800. Fitting labour: 8-12 hours at £65/hr indie rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common engine problems on the XC40 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most frequently reported issues vary by engine. T3 (three-cylinder): Premature main bearing failure causing crankshaft movement and requiring full engine replacement. T4 (four-cylinder): Injector failure causing cold-start misfires; ignition coil faults triggering limp mode. T5 (four-cylinder): Carbon buildup on intake valves; timing chain tensioner wear on early examples.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volvo XC40 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends entirely on your XC40's value and condition. As a rule of thumb: vehicle worth under £10,000 - a used engine or repair typically makes more sense; vehicle worth £10,000-£18,000 - reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years; vehicle worth £18,000+ - rebuilt engine with warranty is usually the best long-term value. For a well-maintained XC40 with a sound body and transmission, engine replacement is almost always cheaper than buying a comparable replacement vehicle.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volvo XC40 petrol engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical XC40 petrol engine swap takes 2-5 working days, depending on the workshop's workload and whether supply-only or supply & fit is chosen. Supply-only: 1-3 days for delivery. Supply & fit: 3-5 days total (including delivery and fitting). Mobile fitting: may take longer as the fitter travels to your location.

mainEntity.name: Which XC40 petrol engine is the most reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The four-cylinder T4 (B4204T47) is generally considered the most reliable of the three. The three-cylinder T3 has a known main bearing failure issue that has been documented on owner forums. The T5 is reliable but requires regular maintenance to prevent carbon buildup.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo XC40 T3 / T4 / T5 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volvo XC40 launched in 2017 as the brand's first compact SUV on the new Compact Modular Architecture (CMA) platform. At launch, the petrol range consisted of 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbocharged units in T3 (156hp), T4 (190hp) and T5 (247hp) forms. A downsized 1.5-litre three-cylinder T3 arrived in 2018 as a direct replacement for the 2.0 T3. The T4 and T5 later gained 48V mild hybrid technology, becoming the B4 and B5 models.

milestones.description: XC40 launches with 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrols: T3 (B4204T37, 156hp), T4 (B4204T47, 190hp) and T5 (B4204T14, 247hp)

commonProblems.h2: Volvo XC40 T3 / T4 / T5 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The XC40 petrol range is generally reliable, but several failure patterns have emerged. The **three-cylinder T3** has been reported to suffer from catastrophic main bearing failure, while the **four-cylinder T4 and T5** engines face carbon buildup, injector and ignition coil issues. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Main Bearing Failure - Why the Volvo XC40 T3 Three-Cylinder Engine Fails Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The three-cylinder T3 engine has been reported to suffer from premature main bearing wear, causing the crankshaft to move excessively (floating crankshaft). The thrust bearing fails, allowing the crankshaft to move in and out, which can trash the entire engine. This is a known issue documented on owner forums.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, full engine replacement, upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: The only option if bearing failure has caused extensive damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of thrust bearings and crankshaft if salvageable
repairOptions.longevity: Only if caught early before crankshaft damage occurs

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical XC40 T3 (2018-2020) is worth approximately £12,000-£22,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. A rebuilt engine at £3,500-£5,500 is a significant but justifiable expense relative to vehicle value. For higher-mileage examples, evaluate the car's overall condition before committing.
problems.recommendation: The T3 main bearing issue is a known design weakness. If you're experiencing any unusual noise, clutch pedal feel changes, or difficulty engaging gears, have the car inspected immediately. If caught early, thrust bearing replacement may be possible. Once damage is extensive, full engine replacement is the only option. A rebuilt engine with upgraded bearings is the definitive fix.

problems.h4: Misfire and Injector Issues - Why the Volvo XC40 T4 Petrol Loses Power
problems.rootCause: The T4's direct-injection system can suffer from injector failure, leading to cold-start misfires. A small amount of fuel left on the injector tip during engine shutdown can cause issues. Ignition coil faults are also common, triggering reduced engine performance (limp mode).

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if only one injector is affected
Recommended if multiple injectors show issues
Fixes misfire and limp mode issues
Only if injector failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Injector and coil repairs (£150-£1,400 specialist) are well within the value of any XC40. These are maintenance items, not replacement triggers.
problems.recommendation: If your T4 is misfiring when cold or under acceleration, start with ignition coil diagnosis - it's the cheaper and more common fix. If that doesn't resolve the issue, injector replacement is the next step. Don't ignore misfires; prolonged driving can damage the catalytic converter.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup - Why Direct-Injection Petrol Engines Lose Performance
problems.rootCause: Direct-injection petrol engines do not have fuel washing over the intake valves, allowing carbon deposits to build up over time. This restricts airflow, leading to reduced performance, rough idle, and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits

repairOptions.specialistPrice: N/A (carbon buildup alone does not justify full replacement)
repairOptions.longevity: Carbon buildup is a maintenance issue, not a replacement trigger

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Carbon cleaning (£400-£800 specialist) is inexpensive relative to any XC40's value. This is a maintenance item, not a replacement trigger.
problems.recommendation: If your XC40 petrol feels sluggish or has a rough idle, carbon cleaning is a cost-effective solution. Use premium fuel and occasional Italian tune-ups to help reduce the rate of carbon buildup.
